The case deliberately checks the source-level visual contract, contrast pairs and stable UI hooks, not pixel output or exact spacing, so future refinements remain possible. M40: the running stage spins. The keyframes and the `animation:spin` shorthand are pinned beside the existing `@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce)` fragment, and the limit of that is stated rather than implied: the adapter runs three INDEPENDENT substring tests, so it grades that all three strings are present and nothing about their relationship. Narrowing the reduced-motion block from `*,*::before,*::after` to `*` would leave the spinner — an `::after` pseudo-element — animating under `prefers-reduced-motion:reduce` with all three fragments still matching and this case still green. Pinning the strings is worth doing and is not the guard the sentence would like to be; a real one renders the page under an emulated reduced-motion preference and reads `animationName`, which is a case nobody has written. The three new ids are the page view beside the trace. Watched red against the pre-M40 page (HEAD before this commit): the case reports FAIL, as does its M40-widened twin ui-execution-progress-is-trace-derived. M40 owner amendment 2: `[hidden]{display:none!important}` is pinned because this page's own layout rules outrank the attribute's UA default — `.status-line{display:flex}` and `.progress{display:grid}` both kept rendering while the DOM reported `hidden === true`, so the idle page view showed a RUNNING chip with the spinner over an empty progress rail.
